summary: Round 29 plan check, 20:18-20:35Z 28 Sep. State: the newest poll header, 20:13:02Z, shows 56640366 PENDING (L > 7.96 h). 31 timer.sh waiters are alive (22:47Z 28 Sep to 00:07Z 30 Sep), as are the 51 watcher (COMPLETE|ERROR), the E10/FEED signal watchers and the battery/poll watchdog. R28-A2 was logged pre-score at 20:18Z. All G4 strings exist, and no past submission carries a night token. Two defects must be fixed before the freeze. (1) The stored R27N-3 G4 freeze check is now vacuous: grep -cF 'W4 FREEZE: NIGHT 29 Sep' already returns 1 because of the R28-A2 (d) line itself. (2) The freeze and batch waiter texts point only to R27-A4/R27N-2/R27N-3, so the R28-A4 fixes (guarded T54, nb_try exit 3, 10.75 h admit edge, item (5)) exist only in round28/report.json. For the morning: the 07:23Z waiter text would build exp89l only after P reads, which would likely miss the 08:40Z A-M1 header. MORNING TABLE v1.1 also contradicts itself on A-M2 (Rr '+' -> exp89q carries DIS, while (1) says only DIS '+' keeps DIS). Missing mechanics: the UP-test S0 for P, since uptest.py cannot read the e10 snapshots; LATE checks between 01:30Z and 06:07Z; a push for late-evening morning reads. New fact: the RULE v2.1 compute anchor is not ambiguous, because 'mode = candidate' and 'GPU shard 0' carry the same timestamp in all 6 dummy logs. exp89l's expected compute is ~1,475-1,500 s (PASS < 1,620). Still true: no E10 trigger; rank 140 at 20:18Z with 127 teams >= 0.959; R28-A5 card edits pending.

findings.what: The G4 freeze check in the stored night batch is VACUOUS. R27N-3's G4 loop (round27/scan_hyp_nightdry.json) and the 00:04Z waiter ('with the R27N-3 guards') count the freeze with grep -cF 'W4 FREEZE: NIGHT 29 Sep' CONTEXT.md. That count is already 1 at 20:25Z, before any freeze exists, because the R28-A2 (d) text at CONTEXT l.4125 quotes the literal. The hardened regex '^- 2026-09-2[89] [0-9:]+ UTC, W4 FREEZE: NIGHT 29 Sep' correctly returns 0. A batch or backup that runs the stored -F check would treat the missing freeze as present, skip the R28-A2 (c) no-freeze fallback, and look for STACK in the wrong line.
findings.evidence: grep -cF 'W4 FREEZE: NIGHT 29 Sep' CONTEXT.md -> 1 (l.4125, inside the 20:18Z RULE v2.1 entry); grep -cE '^- 2026-09-2[89] [0-9:]+ UTC, W4 FREEZE: NIGHT 29 Sep' -> 0; round27/scan_hyp_nightdry.json R27N-3 G4 loop; timer.sh 00:04Z waiter text 'with the R27N-3 guards'. The other G4 strings are all >= 1 (RISK STACK 1, exp89p GATE 1, exp75 LINE 1, exp87a/exp83c 1, R8 night 2, R8 PC19-11 1).
findings.action: In the batch text used at 00:04Z, the 00:20/00:44/00:50/01:30Z steps and post-wake, replace the G4 freeze item with FZ=$(grep -E '^- 2026-09-2[89] [0-9:]+ UTC, W4 FREEZE: NIGHT 29 Sep' CONTEXT.md | tail -1); [ -n "$FZ" ] && echo FREEZE_OK || echo NO_FREEZE. Read STACK only from the entry that starts at that line. NO_FREEZE -> the R28-A2 (c) fallback. Remove the freeze string from the -F loop and keep the other six strings. At 23:33Z write the header with the real time, not '23:30', through the usual entry() helper, so the line reads exactly '- 2026-09-28 HH:MM UTC, W4 FREEZE: NIGHT 29 Sep (...'. Then re-run the regex and expect 1.

findings.what: The 07:23Z MORNING PREP waiter text contradicts R28-A2 (b) and R28-A3 (3) on exp89l timing. The waiter says 'build/dummy exp89l only on branch A with P +/0u', i.e. after exp89p reads (07:46-07:58Z). The logged rule is: build and push the dummy at 51's read in branch A, with a PASS before the A-M1 header (latest 08:40Z). findings.what: MORNING TABLE v1.1 contradicts itself on DIS in A-M2. Clause (1) says 'Only DIS + keeps DIS 2.25 in a morning file; 0, - and ? drop it (winners only)'. Clause (2) A-M2 says 'DIS + -> exp89s; else Rr + -> exp89q', and exp89q = K + SEC + DIS 2.25. Realistic case: exp87a 0.959, P 0.959, exp89r 0.960. Then Rr is '+' but dd = (0.960 - 0.959) - (0.959 - 0.958) = 0, so DIS is '?'. The table sends exp89q, while (1) forbids DIS. The session deciding at ~09:30-11:00Z would pick a row after seeing the reads, which is post-hoc. A worse case: DIS '-' (dd <= -0.002) together with Rr '+' is possible when SEC is large, and the table would still send exp89q.

findings.action: Log a pre-score precedence line before any night read, best inside the freeze line: 'MORNING TABLE v1.1 precedence (pre-score): the A-M2 Rr row is an explicit exception to (1). exp89q goes as the non-CI twin of a stack whose own display won (Rr +), unless DIS = -, in which case A-M2 is UNUSED. The winners-only sentence of (1) governs the new builds (exp89s, exp89t), not the twin.' If the main session prefers the strict reading instead, log 'A-M2 Rr row applies only when DIS is +' before the reads. Either way, fix it before 07:00Z.

findings.what: The UP-test mechanics for the night reads are unstated, and the e10 backup path does not work as written. P '0u' (branch A, which decides A-M1 exp89l) needs an S0 with our count 53 taken before exp89p completes (~07:46-07:58Z) and an S1 with count 54. GAP RULE v2 (4) says to 'use the e10_watch snapshots' as backup. tools/uptest.py load() reads only _lb/<tag>/*.zip or *.csv, while the e10 snapshots are .txt files, so the backup path fails as written. A missing S0 makes the read BLIND, P becomes '0', and A-M1 is UNUSED. Side fact: the LB CSV LastSubmissionDate is the newest SCORED submission, not the best (S1_0934Z shows 00:50:37 = probe 49 at 0.955 while the best was probe 48's 0.957). It flips to 12:14:57 when 51 scores whatever the score, so it marks a completion, never an UP.

In branch B P's UP is not used. (b) For the e10 backup, use a converter that makes no API call: python -c "import pathlib as p,sys;t=p.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding='utf-8');s=t.split('======== leaderboard_rows ========')[1].split('======== histogram')[0].splitlines();i=[k for k,l in enumerate(s) if l.startswith('Rank,TeamId')][0];d=p.Path('experiments/lb_poll/_lb/E10_'+p.Path(sys.argv[1]).stem);d.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);(d/'lb.csv').write_text(chr(10).join(l for l in s[i:] if l.strip())+chr(10),encoding='utf-8')" experiments/e10_watch/<TS>.txt; then python tools/uptest.py compare E10_<TS0> E10_<TS1>. Rows below 0.953 are missing, which does not matter for an UP inside the 0.958 block. (c) At post-wake 06:07Z, if S1_51 is missing, run python tools/uptest.py save S0_night (1 call).

findings.what: The RULE v2.1 compute anchor is NOT ambiguous. In every dummy log, the 'V1284 head patched ... mode = candidate' line and the 'GPU shard 0' line carry the same timestamp (within 1 ms), so R28's anchor worry is moot. Computes (last log time - anchor): exp89r 1,473 s, exp87a 1,569 s, exp89p 1,059 s, exp89q 1,057 s, exp85a 1,126 s, exp89s 1,129 s. CI adds 416-443 s, so the expected exp89l compute is ~1,475-1,502 s: PASS under 1,620 s. Whole-kernel = setup (253-519 s seen; up to 788 s) + compute, which can exceed 2,100 s and then passes by the compute clause. The scratchpad gate85.py still checks only whole-kernel <= 1,900 s and has no compute, Secondary, COORDINJECT or integer checks, so it must not be used for the exp89l gate.
